chunks: And from him, from Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf, from some of our companions, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who died and left a young child, for whom a wet nurse was hired, saying: 'The wage of the child's nursing is taken from what he inherits from his father and mother, and indeed it is his share.'

key_terms.فَاسْتُرْضِعَ: For whom a wet nurse was hired

ai.seo_question: How are the nursing expenses of a deceased father's infant child paid from inheritance according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes that the cost of wet nursing is a direct charge against the infant’s inheritance share, treating it as the child's rightful portion (*hazhhu*) rather than a separate debt. This principle underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that maintenance expenses for minor heirs are prioritized deductions from their estate before distribution, ensuring their immediate care is funded by their own assets.
